summary: Apache HTTP Server is a traditional web server that processes incoming requests and delivers web pages and assets over HTTP. It provides standard web hosting capabilities and adheres to current internet networking specifications. You can run it directly on your operating system or package it inside containers.
goodFor: It suits administrators who need a standard, well-documented web server for publishing static sites or basic HTTP content. It is also useful in environments already standardised around Debian packages or containerised workflows.
watchOut: The upstream release data and repository metrics for this specific entry are unavailable or unrated, meaning you should verify its current maintenance status independently. Configuration syntax can also be complex compared to newer alternatives.
deployNotes: You will typically deploy it using standard package managers or container runtimes like Docker, relying on persistent storage for your web root and log files. It usually sits behind or alongside existing infrastructure, though you will need to configure TLS termination separately depending on your setup.
